trigger: A FIFTH unique sequential_b2 judgment cell (65339dc789ff0340f952cfa75191910e911895baa19ac1e6a3be018cf0e13a32) reached checker_malformed (gemma-4 query_checker, ledger sequences 1415-1416, finish_reason=length, completion_tokens=4096, no result row; its sibling first-query checker call at sequences 1061-1062 completed healthily at 2,612 tokens). Five unique terminal cells in one condition at 5/192 = 2.6% crosses the amendment-5 concentration bound (>=5 cells in a judge/condition at >2%), which is frozen as never relaxable mid-run: the run stops for owner review and this record does not resume it.

material_finding.observed_rate: 5 runaway calls across 117 executed checker calls = 4.3% per call, roughly FOUR TIMES the ~1% the judgment screening measured on pilot-bank-shaped probes (gemma4-checker 0-of-96 at stage 2, max completion 46% of cap)
material_finding.content_dependence: the canary's checker prompts embed LIVE judge queries composed mid-debate by Qwen3.8 and Llama, a different content distribution from the screening bank's protocol-composed probes; the runaway rate is prompt-content-dependent, so the screening pass under-predicted the operational rate (P(0-of-96 at 4.3%) is about 1.5%, so sampling luck alone is an unlikely full explanation)
material_finding.projection: at the observed per-call rate the full 192-cell sequential_b2 condition projects roughly 13-16 terminal cells, which would also cross the 4% affected-mirror-unit bound; the run could not have converged within the frozen bounds even absent the concentration stop
material_finding.mechanism: the same per-prompt-deterministic gemma-4 runaway that excluded its judge_verdict role (amendment 8), now measured at operational scale in its retained checker role
